nodes.content: Characterize when heterogeneous treatment effects remain partially identifiable with weak instruments and bounded exclusion violations in observational healthcare.
requirements: Achieve at least 95% confidence-set coverage uniformly over specified instrument-strength and exclusion-violation classes.
Establish sharp identification bounds and characterize when they improve upon bounds without instruments.

nodes.content: Use subgroup response-type linear programs and exact 95% multinomial projection for sharp bounded-exclusion bounds, benchmarked against no-instrument bounds.
Which subgroup first-stage strengths and exclusion budgets yield response-type bounds strictly narrower than no-instrument Manski bounds?
In HealthSim-1, first-stage ≥0.20 and exclusion-risk budget ≤0.02 yield ≥10% narrower subgroup LP bounds than no-instrument bounds.
Simulate HealthSim-1 across first-stage 0–0.30 and exclusion budgets 0–0.05; compare subgroup LP widths against Manski bounds.
On HealthSim-1, subgroup LP bounds were at least 12% narrower than Manski bounds for first-stage ≥0.20 and exclusion budget ≤0.02.
Retain the full weak-instrument grid for coverage testing, but prioritize ≥0.20 first stages for ≥12% simulated width gains.
Prove LP sharpness; validate uniform 95% exact-projection coverage across first-stage 0–0.30 and exclusion budgets 0–0.05, prioritizing ≥0.20 Manski comparisons.
Enumerate response types to certify sharp LP endpoints; simulate 10,000 HealthSim-1 cohorts per grid cell for exact-projection coverage.
HealthSim-1 validation dossier with sharpness certificates, 10,000-cohort-per-cell coverage tables, and subgroup LP-versus-Manski width maps.
Audit dossier sharpness certificates and 10,000-cohort coverage tables, flagging grid cells below 94.5% and checking prioritized Manski-width gains.
Audit confirmed sharp LP endpoints and uniform ≥95% exact-projection coverage; HealthSim-1 minimum was 95.2%, with ≥12% prioritized width gains.
Use HealthSim-1 dossier's sharpness certificates to stress-test 95% coverage and Manski-relative width under sparse cells and nonlinear violations.
At first-stage 0.03, concentrated nonlinear violations within the pooled 0.02 exclusion budget yielded 92.8% subgroup coverage, refuting uniform validity.
Retain sharp LP bounds, but replace pooled exclusion budgets with subgroup-specific budgets and rerun weak-instrument coverage checks.
Construct subgroup-specific exclusion-budget response-type LPs with simultaneous multinomial projection for sharp bounds, weak-IV coverage, and no-instrument comparisons.
Can subgroup-specific exclusion budgets restore ≥95% coverage at first-stage 0.03 without erasing LP gains over Manski bounds?
Subgroup budgets ≤0.02 restore ≥95% minimum coverage at first-stage 0.03 while preserving ≥5% width reduction versus Manski bounds.
Rerun 10,000 HealthSim-1 cohorts at first-stage 0.03 with subgroup budgets ≤0.02 and concentrated violations; assess coverage and Manski-relative width.
In HealthSim-1, first-stage 0.03 and subgroup budgets ≤0.02 yielded 95.1% minimum coverage and 6% narrower bounds than Manski.
Extend validated subgroup-budget LPs across first-stage 0–0.30 and budgets 0–0.05; prove sharpness, verify ≥95% coverage, map Manski improvements.
Certify subgroup LP sharpness by response-type enumeration; simulate 10,000 cohorts per grid cell, testing coverage and Manski widths.
Subgroup-budget validation atlas: response-type sharpness certificates, 10,000-cohort-per-cell coverage tables, and first-stage/budget maps of Manski-relative bound widths.
Construct exclusion-and-IV-confounding sensitivity polytopes; project exact multinomial regions onto sharp subgroup effects, comparing widths against Manski under weak instruments.
How much instrument–outcome confounding can sensitivity polytopes tolerate before subgroup bounds lose their Manski-width advantage at first-stage 0.03?
At first-stage 0.03, confounding risk-difference budgets ≤0.01 preserve ≥3% Manski-relative width gains under subgroup exclusion budgets ≤0.02.
Extend r2's certified polytopes with confounding budgets 0–0.02; test Manski-relative widths at first-stage 0.03 under subgroup exclusion ≤0.02.
HealthSim-1 sensitivity polytopes retained 3.4% Manski-relative width gains at first-stage 0.03, confounding budget 0.01, exclusion budget 0.02.
Use r2's Manski-width maps to test sparse HealthSim-1 subgroups at first-stage 0.03, exclusion ≤0.02, confounding ≤0.01 for ≥3% gains.
Sparse HealthSim-1 subgroups (n=80) showed only 0.8% Manski-relative width gains at first-stage 0.03, confounding 0.01, and exclusion 0.02.
Retain confounding-sensitive polytopes, but restrict ≥3% width-gain claims to evaluated nonsparse subgroups; report n=80 results separately.
At first-stage 0.03, exclusion ≤0.02 and confounding ≤0.01 preserve ≥3% Manski-relative confidence-set width gains only for subgroups n≥400.
Using r2's sharpness certificates, simulate HealthSim-1 subgroups n=80,200,400,800 at first-stage 0.03; compare Manski-relative confidence-set widths with confounding/exclusion budgets 0.01/0.02.
HealthSim-1 confidence-set width gains were 0.8%, 2.1%, 3.2%, and 3.6% for subgroup n=80, 200, 400, and 800.
Prove sharp confounding-sensitive bounds and uniform ≥95% projection coverage across weak-IV grids; validate ≥3% Manski gains for n≥400.
Extend r2's response-type certificates to confounding polytopes; simulate 10,000 cohorts per weak-IV cell, auditing coverage and n≥400 Manski gains.
Confounding-sensitivity atlas containing sharpness certificates, 10,000-cohort weak-IV coverage tables, and n≥400 Manski-relative confidence-set width maps.
Calibrate subgroup exclusion budgets using negative-control outcomes and capped bias ratios; project joint 95% multinomial regions through sharp response-type LPs.
What clinical-to-negative-control bias-ratio cap preserves ≥95% subgroup coverage and narrower-than-Manski bounds at first-stage 0.03?
With valid negative controls and n≥400, bias-ratio caps ≤1.5 yield ≥95% coverage and ≥2% Manski-relative narrowing at first-stage 0.03.
Using r3, simulate valid negative-control calibration at first-stage 0.03 and n≥400; assess coverage and Manski-width gains for caps 1.0–1.5.
With valid controls, HealthSim-1 minimum coverage was 95.1% and Manski-relative width gains 2.4% at cap 1.5, n=400.
Stress-test r3-based calibration when negative controls share treatment effects or understate exclusion bias by 25%, tracking coverage at cap 1.5.
Valid controls with 25% underestimated calibration budgets yielded 93.8% coverage at cap 1.5 (n=400), exposing plug-in uncertainty.
Retain valid-control calibration, but replace plug-in budgets with simultaneous upper confidence limits before projecting subgroup LP bounds.
At first-stage 0.03, valid controls, ratio cap 1.5, and n≥800, simultaneous limits yield ≥95% coverage and ≥1% Manski-relative narrowing.
Using r3, simulate 10,000 n=800 cohorts with simultaneous control-budget limits at first-stage 0.03, cap 1.5; assess coverage and Manski widths.
In 10,000 n=800 HealthSim-1 cohorts, simultaneous limits achieved 95.2% coverage and 1.3% Manski-relative width gain at cap 1.5.
Using e10's limits and r3's certificates, vary control prevalence 5%–30% at n≥800; test 95% coverage and ≥1% narrowing.
At 5% control prevalence, n=800 cohorts retained 95.1% coverage but achieved only 0.4% Manski-relative narrowing at cap 1.5.
Keep simultaneous calibration limits for ≥95% coverage, but condition ≥1% narrowing claims on adequate control prevalence; report 5% separately.
Simultaneous limits with valid-control prevalence ≥20%, n≥800, first-stage 0.03, and cap 1.5 yield ≥95% coverage and ≥1% Manski-relative narrowing.
Using r3's certificates, simulate n=800 cohorts with simultaneous limits, control prevalence 20%–30%, first-stage 0.03, cap 1.5; assess coverage/narrowing.
At 20%–30% valid-control prevalence, n=800 HealthSim-1 coverage was ≥95.1% and Manski-relative narrowing ≥1.2% at cap 1.5.
Using r3's certificates, stress-test simultaneous limits at n=800–1,600, control prevalence 20%–30%, first-stage 0.03, cap 1.5; audit coverage/Manski-width.
At 2% outcome incidence, n=800 and 20% valid-control prevalence, coverage was 95.1% but Manski narrowing only 0.6%.
Using r3, vary outcome incidence 2%–15% at n=800–1,600 and 20% controls; assess ≥1% narrowing and ≥95% coverage.
At 5%–15% outcome incidence, n=800–1,600 achieved ≥95.1% coverage and ≥1.1% Manski-relative narrowing with 20% controls.
Restrict ≥1% narrowing claims to outcome incidence ≥5%; retain 95% coverage targets at 2% incidence without promising width gains.
Prove sharp control-calibrated LP bounds; verify uniform ≥95% weak-IV/rare-outcome coverage; map Manski gains only at incidence ≥5%.
Using r3 and e13/e14 incidence strata, certify response-type sharpness; simulate 10,000 cohorts per weak-IV cell for coverage and Manski gains.
Control-calibrated LP atlas: sharpness certificates, 10,000-cohort weak-IV coverage grids, and incidence-stratified Manski-width comparisons.
Audit r4’s sharpness certificates and weak-IV coverage grids for sub-95% cells; verify incidence-stratified LP widths against Manski.
Audit confirmed sharp LP endpoints and 95.1% minimum weak-IV coverage; incidence ≥5% yielded ≥1.1% Manski-relative narrowing.
Adopt sharp, valid-control-calibrated LPs with ≥95% audited coverage; claim Manski narrowing only at incidence ≥5%, reporting 2% separately.
